mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals a demand recovery pattern that boosts cyclical equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months, in the absence of a similar decline in unemployment, signals supply-side disruptions that raise input costs and compress margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month -0.5% AND UNRATE not < previous month -0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 300k for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer demand and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +300k for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3%, signals aggressive tightening amid inflationary pressure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > +0.75% AND CPIAUCSL > previous month +3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months, irrespective of monetary policy stance, signals weakening consumer demand, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < previous month -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 1% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based supply expansion, which boosts earnings for capital goods and construction firms, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month +1% AND HOUST > previous month +1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
